ModMetaData.name: RimLLM Framework
ModMetaData.author: 綠菇
ModMetaData.description: RimLLM Framework — A unified LLM interface and core infrastructure framework for RimWorld. This mod provides a stable and flexible foundation for managing API keys, model caching, and provider configuration, so other mods don't have to reinvent the wheel. It enables seamless integration with major LLM services (Gemini, OpenAI, local-compatible endpoints, and more), improving stability and maintainability of in-game LLM calls. Key Features: 1. Multi-Provider Support: Native support for Google Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Groq, Grok (xAI), Z.ai, OpenRouter, Kimi, MiniMax, Qwen, NVIDIA, Player2, and local-compatible endpoints (OpenAI Compatible — LM Studio, Ollama, etc.). 2. Model Fallback: Refactored into a pure model-level precise fallback chain. Players can configure a primary model and multiple exact fallback models; the framework automatically switches on timeout, rate-limit (429), or connection errors to keep LLM calls uninterrupted. Candidate order follows one of four routing strategies (chain priority, minimum latency, round-robin, or lowest cost), retries back off exponentially with jitter, and the circuit breaker cools down per provider and model so one rate-limited model does not take its healthy siblings with it. 3. AES-256 Encryption: API keys are stored with AES-256 using a random storage key protected by the current OS user, reducing plaintext exposure risk. Legacy device-derived ciphertext is accepted only for migration; new writes use the protected key. This still does not prevent same-process attacks via reflection or memory reading. Caller-assembly verification has been removed: it could not stop a hostile in-process mod, and its first-come-wins ModId binding could lock out the legitimate owner at startup. 4. Thread Safety & Scribe Scheduling: All dictionary operations are guarded with locks. RecordLog updates the in-memory log on the Unity main thread via RimLLMDispatcher, while telemetry file writes (AES + JSON + disk) run on a background single-writer with a 15-second throttle, preventing crashes or TPS spikes caused by background saves. 5. Reasoning Models & Auto Effort: Native support for modern reasoning and thinking models (Gemini 3.7 Flash/3.1 Pro Thinking, OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol/5.5, DeepSeek-V4-Pro/Flash, Grok 4.6, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3, GLM-5.3-Flash, etc.). The layer automatically extracts reasoning_content and thought blocks, wrapping them uniformly in <think>...</think> tags. Reasoning effort is translated into each provider's own wire format, and a model that rejects the parameter is learned from the service response and skipped afterwards instead of failing. 6. Native Tool Calling (Function Calling): Fully compliant with Microsoft.Extensions.AI standards (AIFunction, ChatOptions.Tools, FunctionCallContent) across all providers over the shared OpenAI-compatible protocol, along with RimWorldFunctionInvoker (.AsMainThreadFunctionInvokingClient()) to safely dispatch tool execution onto the Unity main thread. 7. Embedding SDK: A public embedding API backed by Google Gemini, OpenAI, Ollama, or OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so other mods can build semantic search and clustering on top of the framework. 8. Provider Stats: Each provider settings page shows a request success-rate progress bar and an API-side prompt cache hit-rate chart (supports server-side prompt caching, including Gemini via its OpenAI-compatible endpoint). 9. Developer SDK: Everything crossing the boundary is a standard Microsoft.Extensions.AI type (IChatClient, IEmbeddingGenerator) — no bespoke client interface to learn, and no registration step. Includes dynamic streaming control and a cached JSON Schema pipeline that normalizes Microsoft.Extensions.AI schema output into a single OpenAI-compatible dialect, so other mods can integrate LLM services and build Agent tools quickly and reliably. 10. Third-Party Integration: An Integrations settings tab can force other AI mods to route their LLM traffic through RimLLM — currently RimTalk (cj.rimtalk), Auto Translation (seohyeon.autotranslation), Mod Compatibility Checker (modcompatchecker.main), and Simplified Chinese Automation: One (ow1r.scauto). Off by default; when enabled, target mod requests use RimLLM's fallback chain, budget, throttling and usage stats while its own API settings are ignored, supporting streaming dialogue, XML batch translations, and conflict diagnosis. Requires Harmony. 11. Mods Using RimLLM: A settings tab lists the active mods that declare RimLLM Framework as a dependency, and marks which ones (including taken-over mods) have actually called RimLLM this session.
